Generated distribution families

Source: R/generators.R
exponentiated.Rd

Build a new family from a baseline family G through a transformation of its CDF, F(y) = T(G(y)), where T is a CDF on [0, 1]. The density is f(y) = t(G(y)) g(y) for a continuous baseline and P(Y = y) = T(G(y)) - T(G(y - 1)) for a discrete one. New shape parameters are appended to the baseline parameters (renamed with a trailing underscore on a clash). All of them can take regression predictors. Quantiles use the baseline quantile function where T has a closed form inverse.

Usage

exponentiated(base)

kumaraswamy_g(base)

beta_g(base)

mcdonald_g(base)

exp_generalized_g(base)

marshall_olkin(base)

transmuted(base)

record_transmuted(base)

odd_log_logistic(base)

odd_burr(base)

weibull_g(base)

gamma_g(base, type = c("zografos", "ristic"))

topp_leone_g(base)

lindley_g(base)

harris_g(base)

sine_g(base)

dus(base)

km(base)

power_series_max(
  base,
  series = c("geometric", "poisson", "logarithmic", "binomial"),
  size = 2
)

power_series_min(
  base,
  series = c("geometric", "poisson", "logarithmic", "binomial"),
  size = 2
)

Arguments

base

Baseline family (identifier or family object).

type

For gamma_g(): "zografos" or "ristic".

series

Power series type.

size

Binomial series size.

Value

A regcomp_family.

Details

  • exponentiated(): T(u) = u^a (Lehmann alternative, exponentiated-G).

  • kumaraswamy_g(): T(u) = 1 - (1 - u^a)^b (Cordeiro and de Castro 2011).

  • beta_g(): T(u) = I_u(a, b) (Eugene, Lee and Famoye 2002).

  • mcdonald_g(): T(u) = I_{u^c}(a, b) (generalized beta-G, GB1-G).

  • exp_generalized_g(): T(u) = (1 - (1 - u)^a)^b (Cordeiro, Ortega and da Cunha 2013).

  • marshall_olkin(): T(u) = u / (alpha + (1 - alpha) u) (Marshall and Olkin 1997).

  • transmuted(): T(u) = (1 + lambda) u - lambda u^2, |lambda| <= 1 (Shaw and Buckley 2007).

  • record_transmuted(): T(u) = u + p (1 - u) log(1 - u) (Balakrishnan and He 2021).

  • odd_log_logistic(): T(u) = u^a / (u^a + (1 - u)^a) (Gleaton and Lynch 2006).

  • odd_burr(): T(u) = 1 - (1 + (u / (1 - u))^a)^(-b) (Alizadeh et al. 2017).

  • weibull_g(): T(u) = 1 - exp(-a (u / (1 - u))^b) (Bourguignon, Silva and Cordeiro 2014).

  • gamma_g(): Zografos and Balakrishnan (2009) T(u) = P(a, -log(1 - u)), or Ristic and Balakrishnan (2012) T(u) = 1 - P(a, -log u).

  • topp_leone_g(): T(u) = (u (2 - u))^a.

  • lindley_g(): T(u) = u^theta (1 + theta - theta log u) / (1 + theta).

  • harris_g(): survival (theta S^k / (1 - (1 - theta) S^k))^(1/k) (Aly and Benkherouf 2011).

  • sine_g(): T(u) = sin(pi u / 2) (Kumar, Singh and Singh 2015).

  • dus(): T(u) = (e^u - 1) / (e - 1) (Kumar, Singh and Singh 2015).

  • km(): T(u) = e (1 - e^-u) / (e - 1) (Kavya and Manoharan 2021).

  • power_series_max() and power_series_min(): the maximum or minimum of a zero truncated power series number of baseline draws, with series "geometric", "poisson", "logarithmic" or "binomial"; T(u) = C(theta u) / C(theta) and T(u) = 1 - C(theta (1 - u)) / C(theta).

Generators nest, so for example beta_g(kumaraswamy_g("weibull")) gives the beta Kumaraswamy Weibull law.

References

Eugene, Lee and Famoye (2002), Beta-normal distribution and its applications. Comm. Stat. Theory Methods, 31, 497-512. Cordeiro and de Castro (2011), A new family of generalized distributions. J. Stat. Comput. Simul., 81, 883-898. Marshall and Olkin (1997), A new method for adding a parameter to a family of distributions. Biometrika, 84, 641-652. Shaw and Buckley (2007), The alchemy of probability distributions. arXiv 0901.0434. Tahir and Cordeiro (2016), Compounding of distributions: a survey and new generalized classes. J. Stat. Distrib. Appl., 3, 13.

Examples

bw <- beta_g("weibull")
d <- distribution(bw, shape = 1.5, scale = 2, a = 2, b = 0.5)
cdf(d, 1)
#> [1] 0.03725503
kwn <- kumaraswamy_g("normal")
mow <- marshall_olkin("weibull")
ewp <- power_series_max(exponentiated("weibull"), "poisson")
